title: Geometry A – Regents
description: Reason with transformations, proof, similarity, circles, coordinates, and solids.

lessons.title: Points, lines and angle relationships
lessons.reading: Definitions give a proof its starting facts. Segment addition combines adjacent lengths. A linear pair totals 180°, vertical angles are congruent, and triangle interior angles total 180°. A diagram's appearance is not a given.
lessons.worked: A triangle with angles 40° and 65° has third angle 75°.

application.prompt: Two supplementary angles include one of 118°. The other is…
application.explanation: Supplementary angles sum to 180°, so subtract 118 from 180.

vocab.definition: Two angles whose measures sum to 180°.
Having the same shape and size.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Supplementary angles sum to 180°, so subtract 118 from 180.

lessons.title: Midpoints and bisectors
lessons.reading: A midpoint divides a segment into congruent halves. A segment bisector must pass through it but need not be perpendicular. An angle bisector creates congruent angles. A perpendicular bisector makes equal halves and a right angle.
lessons.worked: The midpoint of (−2,4) and (6,0) is (2,2).

application.prompt: A segment bisector makes lengths 3x + 1 and x + 9. Find x.
application.explanation: The halves are equal: 3x + 1 = x + 9, so 2x = 8.

vocab.definition: A point dividing a segment into two congruent segments.
A ray dividing an angle into congruent angles.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The halves are equal: 3x + 1 = x + 9, so 2x = 8.

lessons.title: Compass and straightedge reasoning
lessons.reading: A compass copies distances without numerical measurement. Equal arcs from two endpoints locate points equidistant from them. Joining two such intersections constructs a perpendicular bisector. For angle copying, transfer an arc radius and the chord between its intersections.
lessons.worked: To bisect AB, use the same radius greater than half AB from A and B, then join the two arc intersections.

application.prompt: Why must the compass radius exceed half AB in this construction?
options: To obtain two distinct arc intersections
application.explanation: At exactly half the segment length, the circles meet only once; with a smaller radius they do not meet.

vocab.definition: An exact geometric procedure using specified tools.
A line through a segment's midpoint at 90°.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: At exactly half the segment length, the circles meet only once; with a smaller radius they do not meet.

lessons.title: Translations and reflections
lessons.reading: Rigid motions preserve lengths and angle measures. A translation moves every point by one vector. A reflection places a point the same perpendicular distance across a line. Orientation reverses under a single reflection but not a translation.
lessons.worked: Reflecting (3,−2) across the y-axis gives (−3,−2).

application.prompt: Translate (−1,4) by vector (3,−2).
application.explanation: Add the vector components to the original coordinates.

vocab.definition: A transformation preserving distance and angle measure.
A flip across a line with equal perpendicular distances.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Add the vector components to the original coordinates.

lessons.title: Rotations and compositions
lessons.reading: A rotation turns points through an angle around a fixed center. About the origin, 90° counterclockwise maps (x,y) to (−y,x). In a composition, order matters; apply the specified first transformation before the next.
lessons.worked: Rotating (2,5) by 90° counterclockwise produces (−5,2).

application.prompt: A 180° rotation about the origin maps (−3,1) to…
application.explanation: A half-turn reverses both coordinate signs.

vocab.definition: A turn by a fixed angle about a fixed center.
Successive application of transformations.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: A half-turn reverses both coordinate signs.

lessons.title: Symmetry and congruence
lessons.reading: A figure has symmetry when a transformation maps it onto itself. Congruent figures can be mapped using rigid motions. Match corresponding vertices in order before comparing sides and angles; naming order communicates the correspondence.
lessons.worked: A non-square rectangle has 180° rotational symmetry but not 90° rotational symmetry.

application.prompt: Which transformation always preserves congruence?
application.explanation: A translation preserves every distance and angle, unlike a non-unit dilation or stretch.

vocab.definition: Reflection symmetry across a line.
The matching of parts between figures.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: A translation preserves every distance and angle, unlike a non-unit dilation or stretch.

lessons.title: Prove triangles congruent
lessons.reading: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, and the right-triangle hypotenuse-leg condition can establish congruence. SAS requires the included angle. AAA establishes similarity, not equal size. Unspecified SSA does not establish a unique triangle.
lessons.worked: Two side pairs and their included angles establish SAS congruence.

application.prompt: Which is sufficient for triangle congruence?
application.explanation: The included angle fixes the relative placement of the two specified sides.

vocab.definition: A sufficient set of facts establishing triangle congruence.
The angle between two named sides.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The included angle fixes the relative placement of the two specified sides.

lessons.title: Build a logical proof
lessons.reading: A proof links givens to a conclusion through justified steps. Shared sides are congruent to themselves by the reflexive property. After proving triangles congruent, corresponding parts can establish a requested equality.
lessons.worked: A diagonal shared by two triangles supplies a congruent side pair without an extra given.

application.prompt: After establishing triangle congruence, why may you equate corresponding angles?
options: All angles in any triangles are equal
Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent
application.explanation: Triangle congruence guarantees equality of matched parts, but the correspondence must be correct.

vocab.definition: A quantity or figure is equal or congruent to itself.
A logically justified argument establishing a conclusion.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Triangle congruence guarantees equality of matched parts, but the correspondence must be correct.

lessons.title: Triangle theorems and centers
lessons.reading: An isosceles triangle has congruent base angles. A midsegment is parallel to the third side and half its length. Angle bisectors locate the incenter; side perpendicular bisectors locate the circumcenter. Their equal-distance properties refer to different objects.
lessons.worked: If a triangle side is 18, its parallel midsegment measures 9.

application.prompt: Which center is equidistant from a triangle's vertices?
options: Any point on an angle bisector
application.explanation: The circumcenter lies on the side perpendicular bisectors and is the circumcircle center.

vocab.definition: A segment joining midpoints of two triangle sides.
The point equidistant from the three triangle vertices.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The circumcenter lies on the side perpendicular bisectors and is the circumcircle center.

lessons.title: Dilations and scale factors
lessons.reading: A dilation from a center multiplies each distance from that center by scale factor k. Positive k preserves angle measures; lengths scale by k, areas by k², and volumes by k³. Congruence is the special case k = 1.
lessons.worked: A dilation by 3 changes length 4 to 12 and area 5 to 45.

application.prompt: A figure's side lengths double. Its area is multiplied by…
application.explanation: Area has two length dimensions, so its scale factor is 2².

vocab.definition: A transformation scaling distances from a center.
The multiplier relating corresponding lengths.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Area has two length dimensions, so its scale factor is 2².

lessons.title: Prove and use similarity
lessons.reading: AA, proportional SSS, or proportional SAS can establish triangle similarity. Use corresponding sides in a consistent order when writing proportions. A parallel line through two triangle sides creates a smaller triangle similar to the whole.
lessons.worked: Sides 3,4,5 and 6,8,10 are proportional with scale factor 2.

application.prompt: Similar triangles have corresponding sides 4 and 10, and 6 and x. Find x.
application.explanation: The scale factor from the first triangle to the second is 10/4 = 2.5, so x = 6(2.5).

vocab.definition: Figures with congruent corresponding angles and proportional sides.
An equality of two ratios.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The scale factor from the first triangle to the second is 10/4 = 2.5, so x = 6(2.5).

lessons.title: Right-triangle similarity
lessons.reading: An altitude to a right triangle's hypotenuse creates two smaller triangles similar to the original. The altitude is the geometric mean of the hypotenuse segments. Match the smaller and larger triangles carefully before using other proportions.
lessons.worked: If the altitude divides a hypotenuse into 4 and 9, h² = 4 × 9, so h = 6.

application.prompt: A hypotenuse altitude divides the hypotenuse into lengths 3 and 12. Its length is…
application.explanation: The altitude satisfies h² = pq = 36; choose the positive length.

vocab.definition: For positive a and b, the number √(ab).
A perpendicular segment from a vertex to the line containing the opposite side.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The altitude satisfies h² = pq = 36; choose the positive length.

lessons.title: Pythagorean and special triangles
lessons.reading: In a right triangle, a² + b² = c² with c the hypotenuse. A 45-45-90 triangle has side ratio 1:1:√2, and a 30-60-90 triangle has ratio 1:√3:2. Use exact radicals when requested.
lessons.worked: A square of side 7 has diagonal 7√2.

application.prompt: A right triangle has legs 8 and 15. The hypotenuse is…
application.explanation: The sum of squared legs is 64 + 225 = 289; √289 = 17.

vocab.definition: The side opposite a right triangle's right angle.
A right triangle with useful fixed side ratios.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The sum of squared legs is 64 + 225 = 289; √289 = 17.

lessons.title: Sine, cosine and tangent
lessons.reading: Relative to an acute angle, sine is opposite/hypotenuse, cosine is adjacent/hypotenuse, and tangent is opposite/adjacent. The hypotenuse stays fixed, but opposite and adjacent change when the reference angle changes.
lessons.worked: For opposite 3 and hypotenuse 5, sin θ = 3/5.

application.prompt: Relative to θ, opposite is 5 and adjacent is 12. tan θ equals…
application.explanation: Tangent compares the opposite leg with the adjacent leg.

vocab.definition: The opposite-leg to hypotenuse ratio in a right triangle.
The opposite-leg to adjacent-leg ratio.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Tangent compares the opposite leg with the adjacent leg.

lessons.title: Solve contextual triangles
lessons.reading: Draw and label a right triangle before selecting a ratio. Angles of elevation and depression are measured from a horizontal line. Inverse trigonometric functions recover angles from ratios. Use degree mode for degree-based problems and round only at the end.
lessons.worked: A 10-meter ladder makes a 60° ground angle; its vertical reach is 10 sin 60°.

application.prompt: A ramp rises 3 meters over a horizontal run of 4 meters. Its angle is…
application.explanation: The known sides are opposite and adjacent, so use inverse tangent of their ratio.

vocab.definition: The upward angle measured from a horizontal line.
A function finding an angle from a trigonometric ratio.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The known sides are opposite and adjacent, so use inverse tangent of their ratio.

lessons.title: Area and nonright triangle relationships
lessons.reading: A triangle's area is one half of two side lengths times the sine of their included angle. More general triangle relationships extend right-triangle reasoning: the law of cosines relates three sides and an included angle, while the law of sines relates corresponding side-angle ratios.
lessons.worked: Sides 10 and 8 with included angle 30° give area (1/2)(10)(8)sin30° = 20.

application.prompt: Two sides 6 and 10 include a 90° angle. Their triangle area is…
application.explanation: Use A = ab sin(C)/2. Here sin90° = 1, giving 6 × 10/2.

vocab.definition: The angle between two specified sides.
c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C for the side opposite C.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Use A = ab sin(C)/2. Here sin90° = 1, giving 6 × 10/2.

lessons.title: Distance, midpoint and partition
lessons.reading: Coordinate geometry connects algebra and geometric reasoning. Distance follows the Pythagorean theorem. A midpoint averages coordinates. To divide a segment in a specified ratio, move the corresponding fraction of the vector between its endpoints.
lessons.worked: One third of the way from (0,0) to (6,9) is (2,3).

application.prompt: The midpoint of (−4,2) and (2,8) is…
application.explanation: Average x-coordinates and y-coordinates separately.

vocab.definition: √((x₂−x₁)²+(y₂−y₁)²).
Divide a segment into parts with a specified ratio.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Average x-coordinates and y-coordinates separately.

lessons.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
lessons.reading: Nonvertical parallel lines have equal slopes. Nonzero finite slopes of perpendicular lines multiply to −1. Horizontal and vertical lines form the exceptional perpendicular pair. Use slope plus a point to write a line equation.
lessons.worked: A line perpendicular to slope 2 has slope −1/2.

application.prompt: A line perpendicular to y = 3x + 2 has slope…
application.explanation: The negative reciprocal of 3 is −1/3.

vocab.definition: Lines meeting at right angles.
For nonzero m, the value −1/m.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The negative reciprocal of 3 is −1/3.

lessons.title: Classify quadrilaterals with evidence
lessons.reading: Use side slopes, lengths, and diagonals to establish a classification. A parallelogram has both opposite side pairs parallel; a rectangle adds right angles, and a rhombus adds four congruent sides. A square has both sets of added properties.
lessons.worked: Diagonals that bisect each other establish a parallelogram, not automatically a rectangle.

application.prompt: Which extra fact makes a parallelogram a rectangle?
application.explanation: A parallelogram with one right angle has four right angles. Equal sides or perpendicular diagonals alone are not enough.

vocab.definition: A quadrilateral with both opposite side pairs parallel.
A quadrilateral with four right angles.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: A parallelogram with one right angle has four right angles. Equal sides or perpendicular diagonals alone are not enough.

lessons.title: Arcs, chords and angles
lessons.reading: A central angle equals the measure of its intercepted arc. An inscribed angle intercepting the same arc measures half as much. Equal chords subtend equal minor arcs. Tangents meet radii at right angles at the point of tangency.
lessons.worked: An inscribed angle intercepting an 80° arc measures 40°.

application.prompt: An inscribed angle intercepts a semicircle. Its measure is…
application.explanation: A semicircle is a 180° arc; an inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc.

vocab.definition: An angle with vertex on a circle and sides along chords.
A line meeting a circle at exactly one point.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: A semicircle is a 180° arc; an inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc.

lessons.title: Circle equations and lengths
lessons.reading: A circle with center (h,k) and radius r satisfies (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r². Convert expanded forms by completing the square. Arc length is rθ when θ is in radians; a sector is the corresponding fraction of the disk.
lessons.worked: A circle centered at (2,−1) with radius 3 has equation (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 9.

application.prompt: What is the radius of x² + y² = 25?
application.explanation: The right side is r², so r = √25 = 5.

vocab.definition: An angle unit defined by arc length divided by radius.
A region bounded by two radii and their included arc.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The right side is r², so r = √25 = 5.

lessons.title: Intersecting chords and secants
lessons.reading: Products of segment lengths relate intersecting chords and secants. For chords inside a circle, one chord's segment product equals the other's. For two secants from an external point, external length times whole length is equal for both.
lessons.worked: Chord segments 3 and 8 have product 24; another chord with one segment 4 has the other segment 6.

application.prompt: Intersecting chords have segments 2 and 12 on one chord, and 3 and x on the other. Find x.
application.explanation: Use 2 × 12 = 3x, so x = 8.

vocab.definition: A segment with both endpoints on a circle.
A line intersecting a circle in two points.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Use 2 × 12 = 3x, so x = 8.

lessons.title: Area and volume relationships
lessons.reading: Area uses square units and volume uses cubic units. Prisms and cylinders have volume Bh; pyramids and cones have Bh/3. A sphere has volume 4πr³/3. Identify whether a given measure is a radius or diameter before substituting.
lessons.worked: A cylinder of radius 2 and height 5 has volume π(2²)(5) = 20π.

application.prompt: A cone and cylinder have the same base and height. The cone's volume is…
application.explanation: The cone formula includes a factor of 1/3 relative to Bh.

vocab.definition: The amount of three-dimensional space occupied.
A plane's intersection with a solid.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The cone formula includes a factor of 1/3 relative to Bh.

lessons.title: Cross-sections, rotations and density
lessons.reading: A solid's cross-section depends on the cutting plane. Rotating a rectangle around one side creates a cylinder. Density is mass divided by volume; population density is people per area. Keep the appropriate units for the context.
lessons.worked: A 12-gram object occupying 4 cubic centimeters has density 3 g/cm³.

application.prompt: A rectangle rotates around one of its sides. Which solid is generated?
application.explanation: The opposite side sweeps a circular surface while the rectangle's width becomes the radius.

vocab.definition: Mass divided by volume, or count divided by an appropriate measure.
A solid generated by rotating a plane region about an axis.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: The opposite side sweeps a circular surface while the rectangle's width becomes the radius.

lessons.title: Model and justify a solution
lessons.reading: A geometric model makes assumptions about shape, scale, and measurement. Decompose composite solids without double-counting overlap. Explain why a chosen formula fits the shape, and check whether the numerical result and units are reasonable.
lessons.worked: A hollow cylinder's material volume is πh(R² − r²), subtracting the inner space from the outer cylinder.

application.prompt: If every length of a solid is multiplied by 3, volume is multiplied by…
application.explanation: Volume scales with the cube of the length factor: 3³ = 27.

vocab.definition: A mathematical representation using geometric objects and relationships.
A solid made from or decomposed into simpler solids.

lessons.practice: Explain your choice using the relationship or evidence in this lesson.
lessons.reflection: Volume scales with the cube of the length factor: 3³ = 27.
